articles.title: The Moon's Darkest Craters Could Power the World's Most Precise Lasers
articles.summary: Imagine a laser so steady it only drifts by one second every 30 billion years! Scientists found that super-cold, pitch-black craters on the Moon are perfect for building these amazing lasers. They could help us navigate on the Moon and even hunt for hidden space ripples.

articles.title: Happy 100th Birthday, David Attenborough! Here Are 10 Cool Creatures Named After You
articles.summary: A zombie-making fungus that controls cave spiders is just one of about 50 living things named after the legendary nature broadcaster David Attenborough. To celebrate his 100th birthday, meet ten of these amazing plants, animals, and even a prehistoric bird.

articles.title: Is AI Writing All Our Code Now? Inside the Event Where Developers Let Claude Do the Work
articles.summary: At a big coding conference, almost half the developers said they shipped code written entirely by AI—without even reading it! Companies like Anthropic are building AI that can code, test, and fix itself. But some worry: are we moving too fast?
